items.title: 47 - David Rein on METR Time Horizons
items.creator: AXRP, with David Rein of METR
items.description: David Rein explains how METR measures AI ability by the length of tasks models can finish in human working time. It covers the exponential trend and open questions about cost and realism.
items.why_recommended: METR just updated this method today, so this is the best background for it.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A clear sense of what the time horizon metric shows and where benchmarks still fall short.

items.title: The First Mechanistic Interpretability Frontier Lab
items.creator: Latent Space, with Myra Deng and Mark Bissell of Goodfire AI
items.description: The Goodfire team talks about using interpretability to inspect, edit and steer real models. Topics include SAEs versus probes and hallucination detection.
items.why_recommended: It pairs well with today's Anthropic posts on neurons versus SAEs.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: Concrete examples of where SAEs and probes work in practice and where they do not.

items.title: But what is the Fourier Transform? A visual introduction.
items.creator: 3Blue1Brown
items.description: A visual walk through the Fourier transform, built by winding a signal around a circle. It turns a memorised formula into a picture you can reason with.
items.why_recommended: Fourier ideas show up across ML, from positional encodings to signal processing.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A solid mental picture of frequency decomposition.

items.title: Why Every Brain Metaphor in History Has Been Wrong [SPECIAL EDITION]
items.creator: Machine Learning Street Talk, with Mazviita Chirimuuta
items.topic: simplification in science and the mind as computer
items.description: Philosopher Mazviita Chirimuuta asks what science keeps and loses when it simplifies the brain into a model. It traces brain metaphors from hydraulic pumps to computers.
items.why_recommended: It questions the computer metaphor that much of AI and neuroscience quietly relies on.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: Sharper language for when a model of a mind explains and when it only predicts.

cross_domain.connection: It asks whether the abstractions behind neural networks and brain models reveal how minds work or just reflect our own limits.

items.title: If language began in the hands, why did it ever leave?
items.creator: Kensy Cooperrider, Aeon
items.description: A cognitive scientist looks at the idea that language started as gesture before speech. He weighs evidence from children, primates and sign languages.
items.why_recommended: A well-written tour of a deep open puzzle far from daily AI work.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A view of language as embodied, a useful contrast with how LLMs learn from text.
